timeline.event: The Space Shuttle flew in space for the first time.
Enterprise's wing markings were modified to match Challenger.
The Challenger and its crew were lost in a disaster.
A debris strike from ablative material on the right SRB caused significant damage to Atlantis during launch.
Space Shuttle program operating costs were lowered by 21% despite a planned increase in the yearly flight rate for assembly of the ISS.
NASA modified Columbia to fly long missions using the Extended Duration Orbiter pallet.
Columbia flew STS-80, the longest duration flight of the Shuttle Program, lasting over 17 days in orbit.
Thicker reinforced carbon–carbon was installed on the orbiter to prevent damage from micrometeoroid and orbital debris.
STS-93 launched, becoming the first U.S. space mission commanded by a woman, and deployed the Chandra X-ray Observatory.
The seven-member crew of STS-107 was selected.
Seven asteroids were discovered that were later named after the STS-107 astronauts.
A chunk of bipod ramp foam broke away from the ET and hit the SRB-ET attachment ring on STS-112, causing a dent.
Space Shuttle Columbia launched on mission STS-107 from Launch Complex 39A.
Insulating foam separated from the ET left bipod ramp and struck the reinforced carbon–carbon panels on Columbia's left wing.
The Debris Assessment Team held its first formal meeting to examine the launch debris strike.
The Mission Management Team declared the debris strike a turnaround issue and declined to request on-orbit imagery.
Columbia reached Entry Interface at 400,000 feet to begin its re-entry into the atmosphere.
A sensor on the left wing leading edge spar recorded abnormally high strains on the Modular Auxiliary Data System.
The MMACS officer informed the Flight Director that four hydraulic sensors in the left wing were off-scale low.
Mission Control received its last telemetry signal and a broken final communication from the mission commander.
Columbia disintegrated during atmospheric re-entry, killing all seven astronauts aboard.
NASA Administrator Sean O'Keefe convened the Columbia Accident Investigation Board.
President Bush and Laura Bush led a memorial service for the astronauts' families.
ISRO renamed the Metsat-1 satellite to Kalpana-1 in honor of Kalpana Chawla.
Vice President Dick Cheney and Lynne Cheney led a memorial service at Washington National Cathedral.
A memorial service was held at Kennedy Space Center where Robert Crippen delivered a eulogy.
Columbia's flight data recorder was found intact near Hemphill in San Augustine County, Texas.
The OEX recorder tape was delivered to Kennedy Space Center for copying and analysis after inspection and cleaning.
The Houston Astros honored the Columbia crew on Opening Day with seven simultaneous first pitches.
A culture of Caenorhabditis elegans worms that survived the disaster was found alive.
The Columbia Accident Investigation Board released its final report.
The names of the STS-107 crew were added to the Space Mirror Memorial.
timeline.place: KSC Visitor Complex, Merritt Island, Florida

timeline.event: President Bush announced the Vision for Space Exploration, directing the Space Shuttle fleet to retire by 2010.
Super Bowl XXXVIII opened with a pregame tribute to the Columbia crew featuring Josh Groban.
NASA Administrator Sean O'Keefe unveiled a memorial for the STS-107 crew at Arlington National Cemetery.
Congress passed a resolution renaming the Space Science Learning Center to the Columbia Memorial Space Center.
Discovery launched on STS-114, the first Return to Flight mission after the Columbia disaster.
Discovery safely landed at Edwards AFB, after which NASA grounded the fleet again due to foam loss.
NASA's National Scientific Balloon Facility was renamed the Columbia Scientific Balloon Facility.
Discovery launched on STS-121, the second Return to Flight mission.
STS-125 flew the final Space Shuttle servicing mission to the Hubble Space Telescope using Atlantis.
President Barack Obama signed the NASA Authorization Act of 2010, canceling the Constellation program.

legacy.what: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board released its report mandating technical and organizational changes, including on-orbit inspections, recertifying components by 2010, and safe haven/rescue mission procedures.
The United States Board on Geographic Names named Columbia Point, a 13,980-foot peak in Colorado, and the names of the crew were added to the Space Mirror Memorial.
President George W. Bush announced the Vision for Space Exploration, initiating the retirement of the Space Shuttle fleet by 2010 and the development of the Constellation program.
A memorial for the STS-107 crew was unveiled at Arlington National Cemetery, and Congress passed a resolution establishing the Columbia Memorial Space Center in Downey, California.
NASA implemented on-orbit inspections using the 50-foot Orbiter Boom Sensor System and the Rendezvous Pitch Maneuver, and initiated the STS-3xx rescue orbiter contingency program on STS-114.

President Barack Obama signed the NASA Authorization Act of 2010 on October 11, canceling the Constellation program in favor of SLS and MPCV, while NASA made surplus TPS tiles available to educational institutions.
